policy: BLP-004 §7.6 / §13 — regression is measured against this fixed, dated baseline. Changing the baseline invalidates the comparison and forces a re-baseline. The 0.9.0 gate requires delta = 0 (no NEW failures), and every known failure is declared as a limitation.
rebaseline_reason: Ten of the fifteen were FIXED, not waived, in commit 844e323: write_cortex_from_json emitted every generated sigil declaration twice in strict mode, so each glossary entry appeared duplicated in $0 and CODEC-CORTEX rejected the document as E008_DUPLICATE_ENTRY. The first emission loop never recorded the sigil in the `declared` set, so the later 'recompute declarations' block re-emitted all of them. That single defect accounted for all 10 failures in tests/test_cortex_atomic.py and made atomic_write_json(strict=True) produce a different, larger document than write_cortex_from_json(strict=False) — 996 bytes vs 614. Re-baselining is therefore a correction of the record, not a relaxation of the gate: the count went DOWN because real defects were removed, and the five that remain are declared individually below with their cause.
scope: The whole pytest suite at 0.9.0rc3. These five are NOT related to the writer fix. They fail because the fallback column's validator (codec-cortex 0.6.2) rejects ArqUX's own CORTEX dialect systematically: cortex/core/document_kind.py accepts only GSIG/GTYP/GMIC/GCON inside $0, while ArqUX declares its glossary as SIGIL:name{type,weight,focus,desc}, which is flagged E033_ZERO_SECTION_MEMORY_ENTRY. This is not specific to seeded brains — the project brain.cortex, the workspace meta-brain and the identity contracts all fail cortex_verify under this column. It is the same finding BLP-001 recorded: neither column implements the complete CORTEX 0.1 diagnostic contract, and the reference validator is not a usable oracle because it also rejects the 40 valid canonical fixtures (G001). Under the rc1 candidate there is no validator at all.

known_failure_causes.tests/test_blp004_legacy_compat.py::test: expects outcome 'complete', gets 'partial'. Related to HD-01: ArqUX has no execution mechanism at all (zero subprocess/Popen/os.system in src/arqux/handlers/), so the outcome is computed, never earned.
known_failure_causes.tests/test_blp005_entry_content.py::test: expects 2 validation errors, gets 9. The count is inflated by E033 dialect diagnostics that the fallback validator raises on ArqUX's own glossary form.
known_failure_causes.tests/test_blp042_policy.py::TestRecordL: the entry retrieved from $0 is the glossary declaration LNG:lesson{...}, not the recorded lesson, because the dialect conflict places declarations where the lesson should be.
known_failure_causes.tests/test_project_init_onboarding.py::t: seeded brain invalid: 7x E033 for ARQX/DOM/ERR/FCS/IDN/OBJ/WRK declarations in $0, 3x E032 for incomplete FCS/OBJ/WRK.
known_failure_causes.tests/test_sync_brain.py::test_sync_run_: cortex_verify returns valid=False on a freshly synced brain, for the same dialect reason.

resolution_paths: Neither available column can satisfy BLP-004 §13's 'cortex verify --strict with no accepted errors'. Closing these five requires a dialect migration (move the glossary to GSIG/GTYP/GMIC/GCON, which touches every .cortex in the workspace and breaks the rc1 column) or a validator in the rc1 candidate, which is CODEC-CORTEX work rather than ArqUX work. Both are architecture decisions, not release decisions. Tracked as issue 2026-10-11-el-validador-de-la-columna-de-fallback-codec-cor.
verified_on_ci: Run 38167933403 (3.10/3.11/3.12) measured delta 0 against the previous baseline; rc3 re-measures against this one.
